verified_reason: Gallo 2003: abstract text now retrieved (OpenAlex). Double-blind randomised trial, 86 Boca Juniors soccer players aged 18-20 y, creatine (20 g/d for 2 wk, then 5 g/d) vs placebo for 28 wk while "following habitual soccer training"; body mass, anthropometric muscle mass and limb cross-sectional areas, injury incidence and side effects. Conference abstract with results, so not E13. RT is not stated and not ruled out, so it stays maybe under the athlete rule. The abstract appears to be the only report (a 2026 soccer SR, PMC13644428, could not find a full paper): expect E03 at phase 4 under the proposed RT definition unless the authors confirm gym RT; injury data are useful safety context

Kilgore 2002 (JEPonline): no abstract in Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC or OpenAlex, and asep.org is blocked by the proxy. From the title and S2 summary: 5-day loading + 5 wk maintenance during weight training in trained weightlifters, hepatic enzymes. Placebo arm and any body-mass, strength, creatinine or adverse-event data unknown; only the full text can decide (E04 if single-arm, E05 if liver enzymes only)

Thesis (Sim-Anderson 2000, Univ. Alberta), no abstract retrievable (ERA blocked). Author is co-author L.L. Sim of Syrotuik 2000 (SS1-0115), so almost certainly the fibre-morphology arm of that trial; see also SS1-0475. New information: the SS1-0115 abstract gives 37 days of supplementation and training (5-day load + 32-day maintenance), so fibre CSA would fall below the 6-wk hypertrophy minimum. Likely E08 (secondary report of SS1-0115), but the thesis duration is unverified, so keep maybe and decide at full text

Golini 2015: abstract confirms only that Kre-Alkalyn was compared with placebo or creatine monohydrate in several athlete groups (including Bulgarian Olympic weightlifters) using questionnaires and physiological tests; no design, duration, randomisation or training details. Full text (OAT) blocked. Author owns the product (F-COI) and the venue needs a predatory check; likely E15 or E04 at full text, but cannot be decided from the abstract

Trindade 2008 conference abstract (Clin Nutr Suppl P398): no abstract text in Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC or OpenAlex. Title indicates creatine + RT in women with fatigue indicators; comparator, duration and outcomes unknown. Same abstract as SS1-0328, companion SS1-0565: screen the three together and chase a full paper; otherwise E13 or E10

Cribb, Williams, Hayes, Carey 2004: no abstract retrievable. The author list matches the Cribb 2007 trials (SP1-0225 and SP1-0250, both included), so this is probably an earlier abstract or repository copy of one of them and would be E08; it cannot be matched to a specific report without the text. Keep maybe; resolve when SP1-0225/SP1-0250 are read

Cooper 2013 (JEPonline): no abstract retrievable (asep.org blocked). S2 summary: a carbohydrate-protein-creatine product added to 12 wk progressive RT in recreationally resistance-trained men; strength, muscular endurance, body composition. Comparator not stated: E14 if the control lacked the protein and carbohydrate, include if the comparator was matched without creatine. Only the full text can decide. Related: SS1-0295

Khachatryan 2023: abstract confirms creatine monohydrate 0.1 g/kg muscle mass for 28 d in football players with an "Experimental Group" (control implied, not described); speed-endurance test and post-test creatinine, CK, lactate. Randomisation, comparator, age and RT content not stated; athlete sample at 4 wk, so maybe under the athlete rule. Full text may be Armenian or Russian (then E12); venue needs a predatory check

Manna 2016: abstract confirms a randomised trial, creatine 5 g/d vs maltodextrin for 4 wk in 60 male athletes aged 16-19 y; treadmill endurance, heart rate, body mass, body fat, fat-free mass (no change). RT not stated (athlete sample), and the age range straddles 18 with no mean given, so both age (E02 if mainly 16-17) and RT need the full text. OMICS venue: predatory check
E01: rat immobilisation study (title and S2 summary). Confirmed
E07: abstract retrieved (OpenAlex): 24 Navy SEALs randomised to creatine 20 g/d or placebo for 5 days, obstacle-course performance; no RT programme. Confirmed
E02: Brose thesis (McMaster 2001), creatine + RT in older men; parent of Brose 2003 = SP1-0122 (E02); duplicate of SS1-0036 (batch 019, E02). Confirmed

E12: Portuguese-language article (Revista Brasileira de Nutricao Esportiva 2016). Confirmed as non-English, count only. On content it may be an eligible trial (S2 summary: creatine 0.3 g/kg vs placebo, body composition and muscle strength in resistance exercise); design and duration unverified. List as a possibly eligible non-English record
E01: rat study of low-level laser and muscle fatigue; no creatine. Confirmed

E07: abstract retrieved (OpenAlex). Exclusion confirmed but the original reason is inaccurate: the supplemented group took a recovery drink containing amino acids, carbohydrate and creatine monohydrate vs a placebo drink, during one week of high-power squat overreaching (15 sessions) in resistance-trained men; outcomes are squat velocity/power and beta2-adrenergic receptor expression. One week is below the minimum (E07); multi-ingredient vs placebo (E14) and no eligible outcome (E05) also apply. Recode from E03 to E07
E03: abstract confirms HMB vs placebo with 8 wk RT in beginner bodybuilders; creatine kinase only, no creatine supplementation. Confirmed
E02: MSSE 2014 conference abstract, strength training + creatine to prevent sarcopenia in older adults (title); abstract text not retrievable. Confirmed on title
E03: thesis on deer antler velvet supplementation; no creatine. Confirmed
E06: Pediatrics commentary on legal performance-enhancing substances in adolescents. Confirmed
E12: Portuguese-language narrative review (12 articles) of creatine and athlete performance; E06 would apply on content, so not a possibly eligible trial. Confirmed
E01: Arabian horses, creatine with aerobic training. Confirmed
E06: book chapter on nutrition in polymyositis/dermatomyositis (also a clinical population). Confirmed
E06: self-described critical narrative review of nutrition with blood-flow-restriction training; not creatine-specific. Confirmed
E06: narrative paper on nutrition for muscle gain in bodybuilding; no abstract, S2 summary only. Confirmed on title
E12: 1957 Hungarian-journal record (Orvosi Hetilap, PMID 13431262), case report of papillary muscle rupture; no creatine (E06 also applies). Confirmed

E03: thesis (Cooke 2005, Victoria University): creatine monohydrate or whey protein and recovery of muscle function after eccentric damage; supplementation around a single damaging bout, no RT programme (E07 is an alternative). No abstract, S2 summary only. Confirmed
E06: conference lecture summary on sarcopenia diagnosis and management; not creatine-specific. Confirmed

E12 confirmed: OpenAlex returns the abstract in Korean, and every 2016 article of this journal carries the same blanket "en" Crossref tag, many with Korean original titles. Content (from the Korean abstract): 18 soldiers randomised to creatine (n=9) or placebo (n=9) with the same 4-wk combined exercise programme; body composition (no group difference), sit-ups, push-ups, parallel bars, rope climb and urine creatinine. Would be maybe/include if English. List as a possibly eligible non-English trial

E12 confirmed: Korean-language paper (2002), no abstract retrievable. S2 summary: creatine loading vs low-dose creatine during 5 wk strength training in university football players; strength, urine creatinine, body composition; a creatine-free comparison is implied but unverified. Companion of SS1-0011 (batch 019, 7-day report, E12). List as a possibly eligible non-English trial

E12 confirmed: Portuguese-language systematic review of creatine and anaerobic performance (searches SciELO, LILACS, CAPES; double-blind RCTs). It would be an SR/MA mapping record if English; not a trial. Count only; optional citation-chasing source

E13 as recorded; exclusion confirmed with a caveat. No abstract text exists in any reachable source, so "no results" cannot be shown. Same first two authors, sport and outcomes as Kuwamori 2008 (SS1-0029, batch 019, coded maybe), so it is very probably the meeting abstract of that trial and its fate follows SS1-0029: recode E08 if SS1-0029 is included, same exclusion code if not (same handling as SP8-0040). Not treated as a rescue because the trial is already carried as a maybe through SS1-0029

E07: no abstract retrievable (Crossref, Europe PMC, OpenAlex empty); S2 summary says short-term creatine + sodium bicarbonate vs placebo with hormonal and oxidative-stress responses to resistance exercise. Even if longer than stated, the outcomes are not protocol outcomes (E05) and the combined supplement vs placebo is E14. Confirmed

E06 confirmed: review of creatine in gynaecology and women health. The only method stated is a PubMed keyword search ("creatine", "gynecology"); no study-design or eligibility criteria and no count of studies, and the aim covers biology, product forms and preclinical work. Narrative review, same call as SP7-0013
E14: Jack3d multi-ingredient pre-workout vs placebo in resistance-trained men; creatine effect not isolable. No abstract, S2 summary only. Confirmed

E05: urinary chemiluminescence and plasma malondialdehyde with strength training (creatine per S2 summary); oxidative-stress markers only, no abstract. Probably a secondary report of de Souza 2008 (SS1-0165, included): link it and recode E08 if the cohort matches. Confirmed

Larson-Meyer 2000: design now verified. Abstract retrieved (OpenAlex): 14 female collegiate soccer players randomly assigned to creatine (15 g/d for 1 wk, then 5 g/d) or placebo for 13 wk of off-season training; bench press and full-squat 1RM, DXA lean mass. Independent confirmation: PMC13644428 (2026 soccer SR) tabulates it as randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled; PMC11225636 states the off-season training consisted of strength and soccer sessions; PMC8228369 lists one case of nausea. Mean age 19 y. Not in PubMed. Keep include

Syrotuik 2000: design now verified. Abstract retrieved (OpenAlex): 21 men aged 20-26 randomly assigned to creatine load + placebo maintenance, creatine load + 32-day maintenance, or placebo, all doing the same periodised RT; bench press and incline leg press 1RM and lifting volume. Independent confirmation: PMC12430374 (2025 strength MA) tabulates 21 trained men, RT 4 d/wk at 65-95% 1RM. Correction: supplementation and testing span 37 days (about 5 wk), not the 8 wk in the original note, so strength is eligible but any lean-mass or fibre data fall below the 6-wk minimum. Not in PubMed. Keep include; companions SS1-0136, SS1-0475

Self-titled systematic review (Quality in Sport 2025) of creatine monohydrate on strength, muscle mass and training performance. On intervention, comparator and design it passes the SR/MA rule (creatine-specific, RCTs, RT not excluded). But the abstract does not establish a systematic review: the aim cites "case studies, clinical trials and long term research", the method is "review and analysis of randomized clinical trials and clinical studies from 2017 to 2025 available in PubMed", and there are no eligibility criteria, selection flow or count of included studies. Full text blocked. Design unverified: include for mapping if the full text has explicit criteria and a list of included trials, else E06 like SS1-0142

SR/MA mapping: passes the SR/MA rule. Abstract states the database (PubMed), search date (May 2026), date range (2000-2026), eligibility (RCTs in adults 60+ given creatine alone or with RT) and the number included (13 RCTs); creatine-specific and its criteria admit creatine-vs-placebo RT trials. Older population kept for mapping only. Weak methods (single database, no meta-analysis) and an obscure venue: flag for AMSTAR 2 and a predatory check

Poprzecki 2008 (J Hum Kinet): abstract confirms alkaline creatine vs placebo in 23 untrained men, both groups doing RT 3 times a week for 4 wk, then 3 wk follow-up; body mass, body composition, serum creatinine, Wingate power. Randomisation is not stated ("divided into"), but at screening a creatine + RT trial with a placebo comparator is include; allocation is a full-text check. If not randomised, keep for safety outcomes only (ROBINS-I). At 4 wk, body mass and creatinine are eligible; lean mass is below the 6-wk minimum

de Franca 2015: abstract confirms 40 recreational weightlifters in four groups (creatine monohydrate 5 g, creatine HCl 5 g, creatine HCl 1.5 g, resistant-starch control) with 4 wk RT; 1RM leg press and bench press, body composition. A creatine-free control with the same RT is present. Randomisation and blinding are not stated ("divided"); allocation is a full-text check, and if not randomised it is kept for safety outcomes only. Strength eligible at 4 wk; lean mass below the 6-wk minimum. SCIRP venue: predatory check (E15 only if methods cannot be verified)
